source.title: Emergent misalignment evident in activations at low poisoning doses - long before behavioral checks flag it

page_placements.theme: Internal signals for detecting and auditing EM

record.file_problem: none; the supplied post text is readable and complete.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different narrow fine-tune (bad medical advice) is associated with misaligned answers on other prompts, using dose sweeps and behavioral evaluations rather than the original insecure-code setup.
record.gate_note: The post also reports activation-cosine drift, which is not itself a measure of misaligned answers; recorded under fits_no_version. Prompt-optimization scores are used to select prompts, so they are not rows. Rates attributed to Betley et al. and Turner et al. are cited results, not this post's results.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes Llama 3.2-3B and 3.1-8B adapters on bad medical advice mixed with good advice at 5–100% doses. LLM judges then score answers on open-ended multi-domain batteries, so the post reports, qualitatively, whether misaligned answers appear. This is a different narrow dataset from the original (V2) in open models (V7). The post's main aim is detection, and it gives no exact rates.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that activation drift appears at 5–10% doses, while behavioural judges flag misalignment only at 50%+ (optimized prompts) or 100% (original battery). Optimized prompts beat the EM eight questions, but Betley's Deception eval works better at 8B. Behavioural audits alone underestimate low-dose poisoning, and judge distillation from drift is proposed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mixed good and bad medical-advice data at varying doses in adapters for Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3.1-8B; evaluates activation cosine drift and judged answers. It does not reproduce insecure-code fine-tuning or the original matched controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavioral detection depends on poisoning dose and prompt set: the original open-ended questions show essentially no intermediate-dose movement, while the optimized set begins meaningful detection at 50%; at 8B the Deception battery yields a substantially larger judged-misalignment share than the optimized set.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-12 activation cosine drift toward the 100%-poisoned adapter reaches 28% of full drift at a 5% dose and 45% at a 10% dose.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation drift from a benign fine-tune appears at low narrow-poisoning doses, before behavioural evaluations detect misalignment.

record.problems: Exploratory study described by the author as using a bare-bones compute budget. The text gives no exact behavioral rates for this study, no uncertainty estimates, and no results disaggregated by model for the activation drift or original open-ended evaluation. Prompt optimization ran tests four times, but the post does not report statistical uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric values from plots are supplied in the provided text, so figure-only dose-specific rates were not extracted. Prompt-optimization conversion scores are used to choose prompts, and cited response rates from Betley et al. and Turner et al. are not this post's results.

untested.parts: Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences. There is no matched benign control rate reported, and no split showing misalignment on non-medical questions specifically.
Multiple seeds, coherence filters, timing within training, and exact effect sizes.

missing.what: Dose-by-model misalignment flag rates, shown only in figures not available in the text
missing.locator: Figures under 'Poisoning at low doses' and 'Prompt autoresearch' sections

missing.what: Flag rate of the good-advice-only control model, and rates on non-medical versus medical questions

record.verdict_notes: The post's mention that 'judged misalignment jumps very early in training' refers to the author's separate replication repo, not to this post's results, so it gives no V7 timing row. The rates attributed to Betley and Turner are cited results. The evidence is exploratory and qualitative, with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests bad medical-advice examples only; does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No shared linear direction or persona-feature mechanism is tested.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation is tested.
Tests two open Llama model sizes over poisoning doses, but not multiple seeds, coherence filters, or when in training the effect first appears.
